John — per our action item, here's a benchmarking note with assumptions up front.

Assumptions (applies across benchmarks):
- Workload: instruction-following chat, avg response length ~300 tokens, request tokens ~50.
- Throughput/latency target: median latency <600ms per request; 95th <1.5s.
- Production optimizations: batching, KV cache for repeated prefixes, int8 quantization where acceptable.

Benchmarking (indicative $ / 1M tokens, normalized):
- Redwood (optimized infra + quantized model variants, managed): $70 / 1M tokens — includes GPU amortization, infra, caching, and basic 99.9% uptime SLA. (Assumes 8-bit quantized LLM and 35–45% reduction in token cost vs FP16)
- Hugging Face (managed inference): $95 / 1M tokens — higher managed-hosting fee and less aggressive batching guarantees.
- OpenAI (hosted API, comparable capability): $130 / 1M tokens — premium for proprietary models + higher per-request latency SLAs.
- Anthropic (hosted API): $120 / 1M tokens — similarly positioned to OpenAI on price/quality.
- Self-host on GCP (customer-owned infra w/ in-house ops): $40–60 / 1M tokens — lower unit infra cost but requires >FTE ops and no built-in SLA or upgrades.

Notes on variance:
- Quantization and kernel optimizations commonly yield 30–50% savings; batching and KV cache can add another 10–20% effective reduction for our conversational workload.
- Net price available to you depends on contract term, committed capacity, and whether you accept a quantized model variant (we can provide A/B testing on quality).

Recommended commercial approach:
- Pilot (90 days): Redwood-managed PoC at $0.00 for first 200M tokens (trial credit) + $65/1M thereafter during trial to validate quality/latency.
- Production (annual commit): target list price $70/1M with tiered commit discounts — e.g., 10% at 1B/mo commit, 20% at 3B/mo commit.

I've attached the pricing worksheet with line-item assumptions. If this aligns, we can convert the PoC into a formal SOW and send to procurement.

Proposed next steps: 1) Tech/procurement sync Thu Mar 26 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent). 2) Redwood to provision PoC and share metrics dashboard + tooling access. 3) Procurement to send PO template if they have special terms.

Happy to adjust numbers — what matters most is predictable unit economics and clear rollback/quality gates.

— Vanessa
